subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value:
TWO BOUNDARIES ON THE TERNARY-DIAMOND FAMILY, both measured on one TU. Neither supersedes claim.law.IH_ternary-diamond-lever-extends-to-integer-guards.20260901.v1 or claim.law.IT_empty-bodied-if-elides-its-own-comparison.20260901.v1; each closes a sub-case those laws leave open.

(1) THE EMPTY-BODY ELISION EXTENDS TO THE IF/ELSE-WITH-EMPTY-THEN FORM. The IT law establishes that MWCC's front end discards a syntactically empty conditional body whole, and every one of its measurements is on `if (c) { }` with NO else - a statement the compiler can delete outright. That leaves an obvious and tempting sub-case open: `if (c) { } else { BODY }`, where the statement CANNOT be discarded because the else must be emitted, and where one might therefore expect the empty then-arm to survive as the `b` that a forward branch pair needs. It does not. MWCC inverts the guard and emits the single merged conditional branch, exactly as it does for the equivalent `if (!c) { BODY }`. Measured here as NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL - the object bytes did not change at all against a source that already spelled the negated form - so the empty-then-with-else spelling is a strictly null probe, not merely a weak one. Treat the IT law as covering empty conditional ARMS generally, not only empty conditional STATEMENTS, and do not spend a build on this variant. The ternary remains the only carrier that materialises an empty arm block, because a ternary arm is an expression result rather than a statement block.

(2) THE TERNARY LEVER'S COUNT COST IS A PER-FUNCTION REGISTER-PRESSURE PROPERTY, NOT A PROPERTY OF THE SOURCE PATTERN, AND MUST BE RE-MEASURED PER FUNCTION. The IH law's cost note says the rewrite adds one instruction per site and warns to arbitrate on fuzzy rather than count. What that note invites, and what is refuted here, is the inference that the cost is a constant of the pattern which can be predicted once and then applied across matching sites. Two functions in ONE translation unit, with a residual identical row for row and an edit identical character for character, priced it differently: on setWorldParms the five-site rewrite was FREE, holding the instruction count exactly equal at 843/843 while the multiset converged 40t -> 32t, and on MBNewPsysDescrip the same rewrite cost four instructions, 793 -> 797. So a matching residual SIGNATURE does not license transferring a measured cost, and a lever that was free on one function is not thereby free on its twin.

THE ARBITRATION RULE THAT FOLLOWS, and it is the operationally useful half. When the ternary rewrite holds count parity, it is a free structural win: keep it on any non-negative fuzzy. When it breaks count parity, fuzzy alone is NOT sufficient to keep it, and the IH law's 'arbitrate on fuzzy' should be read as necessary rather than sufficient. Weigh the fuzzy gain against what count parity is worth on THAT function: where regnorm shows an overwhelmingly RENAMING residual over few genuine structural rows - 170 of 15 on setWorldParms, 184 of 15 on MBNewPsysDescrip - the realistic route to EXACT is the WebFrank recolor path, for which identical instruction shape is a hard precondition, and spending count parity for a fraction of a fuzzy point forecloses the more valuable option for a gain that does not move project progress at all (measured: All 98.29% fuzzy / 64.42% matched, identical with and without the edit). Reopen such a site only when a lever for the accompanying surplus copies is in hand, so the added instructions can be paid for rather than merely spent.
